key_insight: Trusted quantum communication can be shifted from qubit preparation/measurement to a trusted single-qubit rotation device plus an untrusted provider, with composable security.
engineering_relevance: This reduces hardware trust requirements and supports broader deployment of quantum cryptographic protocols on the Qline and similar architectures.
method: Construct a universally applicable protocol for delegating single-qubit measurement to an untrusted provider.
Design a qubit-preparation construction that works under protocol-specific assumptions.
Show these assumptions are naturally met by most common quantum cryptographic protocols, validating the Qline architecture.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports two composably secure constructions and argues, by protocol analysis, that the preparation assumptions hold for the vast majority of standard quantum cryptographic protocols.
watch_item: The qubit-preparation delegation is not universal and depends on assumptions about the underlying protocol, so compatibility must be checked case by case.
paper_title: On the cryptographic potential of single-qubit rotations
